assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks unite a beautiful quantum-control idea with unprecedented precision and enduring scientific reach.
assessment.attribution: Katori originated the magic-wavelength lattice-clock concept, and Ye made decisive experimental realizations and extensions.
assessment.maturity: Independent clock platforms now demonstrate exceptional accuracy, reproducibility, and broad use in fundamental measurements.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: These effects revealed that quantum phase has directly observable geometric and topological content, transforming quantum physics.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov introduced the physical significance of electromagnetic potentials, while Berry identified the general adiabatic geometric phase.
assessment.maturity: The phenomena have been repeatedly observed and have become foundational across atomic, optical, and condensed-matter physics.
uncertainties: The two concepts are distinct developments, so whether they form one sufficiently unified prize requires careful judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision picture exposed an unexpected strong-field atomic mechanism and opened high-harmonic and attosecond science.
assessment.attribution: Corkum provided the seminal physical model, while Lewenstein supplied a highly influential quantum formulation used throughout the field.
assessment.maturity: Its predictions have been extensively tested and underpin a large, mature experimental field.
uncertainties: The proximity to the already recognized attosecond-light field complicates defining a clearly separate discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their proposals made controlled atomic systems a general route to quantum computation and simulation of otherwise inaccessible many-body problems.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller jointly supplied central theoretical architectures that guided major experimental programs.
assessment.maturity: Trapped-ion processors and atomic simulators have realized key elements over decades in several laboratories.
uncertainties: The broad quantum-information enterprise makes a sharply bounded attribution difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed states turned a quantum limit on measurement into a practical route to enhanced interferometric sensitivity.
assessment.attribution: Caves established the central quantum-measurement principle; Mavalvala and Schnabel made decisive experimental and gravitational-wave applications.
assessment.maturity: Squeezing is now robustly deployed in leading interferometers and confirmed as a real sensitivity gain.
uncertainties: Credit for experimental development spans several closely connected groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-amplified spontaneous-emission X-ray lasers created an entirely new ultrafast, coherent probe of matter.
assessment.attribution: The credited scientists made foundational theoretical and accelerator-physics contributions to the SASE concept.
assessment.maturity: Working facilities have transformed structural, chemical, and ultrafast science for more than a decade.
uncertainties: The achievement depended on large international facilities, making the limited-person attribution intrinsically difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade enabled unusually direct control of strong interactions among individually resolved atoms and a powerful new simulator platform.
assessment.attribution: Saffman developed crucial blockade-gate concepts, while Lukin and Browaeys led landmark experimental implementations.
assessment.maturity: Multiple laboratories now operate large arrays and demonstrate simulation and computing capabilities.
uncertainties: It remains unclear whether the most consequential applications and a stable division of credit have fully matured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry extended matter-wave coherence into an exceptionally sensitive method for testing and measuring fundamental physics.
assessment.attribution: Bordé established key conceptual and optical methods, and Kasevich produced influential precision-interferometry realizations.
assessment.maturity: The methods are well established across many laboratories and applications.
uncertainties: The field has many essential contributors and no single experimental breakthrough is obviously dominant.
